reason: While this text (1 Samuel 9-10) describes the selection and anointing of Saul as Israel's first king with the explicit purpose of delivering the people from the Philistines, it does not establish a prescriptive 'model' of good leadership defined as 'a functioning government to the benefit of the people.' The narrative is descriptive rather than didactic—it recounts how leadership was established but does not articulate principles of good governance. Moreover, the text immediately undercuts any idealized vision by concluding with 'worthless fellows' questioning whether this new leader can actually save them, suggesting skepticism about whether formal governmental structure alone benefits the people. The text narrates institutional change but does not present it as an exemplary model for leadership.
